items.text: Does the design doc have sections on scalability, redundancy and reliability, dependencies (including DNS and time, dependency cycles), data integrity, SLA requirements, and security and privacy (or explicitly state that there are none)?
Was a quick security design review requested after finalizing the design doc?
Are the critical requirements (without which there is no viable product) distinguished from the other feature requirements?
Were security and reliability treated as emergent properties of the whole design and development flow, and not as a module to be added later?
Is there upfront investment in testing, reliable CI/CD, staged rollouts and feature flags (sustained velocity)?
When using third parties (e.g., payments): did you consider not holding the sensitive data, new failure modes, the vendor's posture, proprietary libraries and JavaScript on the web origin?
Were the relevant motivations, profiles (hobbyists, researchers, governments, activists, criminals, automation/AI, insiders) and methods (threat intelligence, kill chain, TTPs) considered?
Were insider scenarios (first-party, third-party, related) generated with actor x motive x action x target?
Are there automatic checks against human configuration errors (the case of the '/' in the malware list)?
Did you cover the basics (e.g., 2FA) before exotic attacks, without assuming that sophistication predicts success?
Are data, APIs and services classified by risk (e.g., public, sensitive, highly sensitive with no permanent access)?
Are administrative APIs small and functional, rather than an interactive session over a large API (POSIX)?
Zero trust: access by user and device credentials, without trusting network location and without ambient authority?
Granular audit logs with structured justification; auditor with context; breakglass review by the team and central auditing of breaches?
Are there least-privilege tests (profiles x scenarios) and a test infrastructure with separate credentials and anonymized data?
Access denials: blind denial for callers without privilege and a token for those with minimal privilege; fast support?
Is breakglass restricted (SRE), accessible from specific locations, monitored and tested regularly?
MPA on sensitive operations, with context for the approvers and real conditions to deny?
For very risky operations, is there approval on a second hardened platform (3FA) against broad workstation compromise?
terms: stronger authorization of a specific request

items.text: Do temporary access, business justifications and proxies/bastions cover the cases without fine-grained control?
Do administrative changes go through a safe proxy or automation (Zero Touch) with logging, MPA and rate limiting?
Are the security and reliability invariants explicit and does each have an owner?
terms: system invariant is a property that is always true

items.text: Are horizontal requirements (authentication, authorization, logging, deadlines) in a central component (framework/library)?
Are interfaces narrow and typed (gRPC, Thrift, OpenAPI) and operations idempotent?
Does every active entity have an understandable, spoofing-resistant and non-reusable identity (an IP is not an identity)?
Is the TCB of each critical property as small as possible and do the boundaries (including web origins) follow the threat model?
Is there an application framework that guarantees a valid authorization policy and denies by default?
Do critical flows use types with a contract (Url, SafeSql, SafeHtml) instead of strings?
Is cryptography done through a high-level library that does not accept raw key material?
terms: does not accept raw key material

items.text: Are security changes incremental, documented, tested, isolated by feature flag, qualified and staged?
Dependencies updated, frequent rebuilds and small releases with automated tests?
Immutable containers, image patching in the registry and monitoring of container age?
Is there a zero-day plan: triage, patch verification, gradual rollout, mitigation, communication and monitoring?
Does the plan cover a broken embargo and regular rotation of keys and secrets?
Is each layer independently resilient (defense in depth)?
Was controlled degradation defined in advance (critical features, what to turn off, security tradeoff)?
Is there load shedding and throttling by priority and cost, with security functions at high priority?
Do critical security operations not fail open; is there a nonnegotiable minimum posture?
Humans in the loop: change budget and protection of the services used in recovery against automation?
Are there compartments by role, location and time, with validation that forbidden operations fail?
Failure domains with isolated data, input validation and last known good configuration?
Do high-availability, low-dependency components exist, are they validated, and do they avoid becoming routine or rotting?
Continuous validation: fault injection, mirroring, split, measured key rotation (latency and verified loss of access)?
Does the update system run at maximum speed, with a rate controlled by policy and an isolated rate limiter?
terms: regular push system turned up to maximum

items.text: No dependence on wall-clock time: epochs, versions or validity lists, with a rate-limit backstop?
Explicit rollback policy (external deny list, SVN/MASVN, signing key rotation) against unzipping?
Explicit revocation without fail open, with a safeguard against mass revocation and without special accounts?
terms: refuse any update that revokes its own

items.text: Is the intended state (host, firmware, global services) encoded and are deviations repaired; has rebuilding from scratch been tested?
Do backups have integrity validated at restore; partial restore; data and key deletion considered?
Emergency access with low dependency, credentials with adequate validity, alternative communication and periodic training?
Layered defenses on the shared infrastructure (edge, load balancers) and router ACLs instead of a stateful firewall in the first line?
Caching, fewer requests and less egress; actionable alerting; graceful degradation; automatic mitigation with fail static?
Do clients use exponential backoff with jitter?
Do frameworks and libraries prevent classes of vulnerabilities by construction (TrustedSqlString, SafeHtml, templates with contextual escaping)?
Memory-safe language, strong typing, strong types for units and sanitizers in presubmit or continuous build?
Simplicity: no deep nesting and YAGNI, technical debt paid down; refactoring never mixed with functional change?
Hermetic unit tests, with security cases, and verification that they would fail without the code (mutation)?
Do integration tests use non-sensitive test data (never mirroring real databases)?
Fuzzing with sanitizers, seed corpus and dictionaries; continuous fuzzing; deterministic and fast drivers?
Fast static analysis in code review and periodic deep analysis; formal methods only where justified?
Mandatory and substantive code review (MPA) for code and configuration?
Build, test and deploy 100% automated and locked down against tampering by administrators?
terms: Move all build, test, and deployment steps

items.text: Does the deploy environment verify the artifact (provenance or signature) and not just who deployed?
Secrets outside version control and code, in secret management or KMS, accessible only to services?
terms: Never check secrets into version control

items.text: Is third-party code reviewed according to trust and are dependencies monitored for vulnerabilities?
Does each build emit provenance with Authenticity, Outputs, Inputs (sources, dependencies, command, environment) and versioning?
Does the per-environment deploy policy evaluate provenance: origin, review, official build, tests, allowed binary, recent version, recent scan?
Hermetic builds (and reproducible when possible) and privilege separation between the trusted orchestrator and user commands?
Does the deploy decision happen at a choke point, with logs for post-deploy verification, actionable messages and rare, audited breakglass?
Structured, immutable and centralized logs, with a retention, privacy and access policy defined with legal?
Log sources covered (OS, host, application, cloud, network, DNS, proxy) with a budget and graceful degradation of storage?
Emergency credentials to debug security systems; protected debug endpoints; metadata treated as sensitive?
Disaster risk analysis with a probability x impact matrix and defined severity and priority models?
IR team with roles (IC, SREs, PR, support, legal, privacy, forensics, security), charter, delegates and champion?
Response plans and playbooks accessible in a disaster, with backup communication (not depending on a system that may be compromised)?
Prestaging: emergency access, logs with long retention, forensic agents, restorable backups, alternative paths and training with an escalation window?
Tests: automation audit, tabletops, fault injection, multi-component failures, full failover, Red Team and postmortem of the tests?
OpSec plan defined before the incident (clean channels, no logging into compromised machines, no locking accounts before understanding the scope)?
IMAG roles (IC, OL, CL, RL), IC loop, shifts of at most 12 h and formal handover with an agenda?

Does the recovery plan answer the five questions (attacker reaction, compromised tools, variants, reintroduction of vectors, mitigation options) and use a checklist with marked quarantine and credential rotation?
Security postmortem with action items with owners, separated into short and long term?
Are the cultures of by default, review, awareness, yes, inevitably and sustainability considered?
Aligned incentives and reduced fear (canary, dogfood, trusted testers, opt-in, progressive stringency, breakglass)?
Is security everyone's responsibility, with embedded specialists (security champions, Red/Blue Teams) and a VRP only after the basics?
terms: basics of finding and addressing regular security issues
